prerequisites: It is recommended that the student has passed the subjects Manufacturing Engineering and Manufacturing Technologies as well as knowledge of design and CNC programming software.

learning_outcomes.text: It is intended that the student becomes capable of designing manufacturing processes, from the geometric conception and modeling of elementary parts to obtaining the final product, based on computer-aided design and manufacturing technologies. Similarly, the aim is for the student to have the necessary resources for simulating such processes and to know and apply, as far as possible, the most current manufacturing technologies.
Acquisition by the student of the basic knowledge and the minimum skills that allow them to address activities and problems related to CAD/CAM/CAE/CIM.

Acquisition by the student of the basic knowledge that allows them to conveniently address problems related to establishing the optimal conditions necessary to carry out a specific manufacturing process, its analysis, evaluation, and improvement of performance from the perspective of process automation.

syllabus_topics: IT Practices Block I: CAD/CAM Integration Lesson 1: Part Operation
Block II: CAM. Advanced Machining Lesson 1: Planing Operation
Machining Operations for Complex Surfaces. Roughing
Machining Operations for Complex Surfaces. Horizontal and Vertical Sweeping
Post-processing Operations, CNC Code Generation, and Machine Preparation

assessment_methods.method: Continuous evaluation: Workshop Practices Block (attendance and submission of practice reports)

assessment_rules: The final grade is based on a 40% CAM block exam, a 40% theoretical block exam, and 20% continuous assessment for workshop practices, which includes attendance and submission of practice reports. Practice reports must be submitted before the start of the evaluation period.
